abstract: Significance Coevolution with endosymbionts enables sap-feeding insects to thrive. Yet, continuous genome reduction in obligate endosymbionts not only challenges their coordination with hosts but becomes a major obstacle for the symbiotic system to adapt to changing environments. The facultative endosymbionts are frequently effective agents in stabilizing the intimate partnership in symbioses, particularly under heat stress. Here, we reported that a complete DNA repair system assembled by components from Buchnera and Serratia , two endosymbionts of aphids, could ensure the genome integrity of Buchnera , and thereby enhanced thermostability of aphid bacteriocytes. Collectively, heat stress might exert substantial selective pressure on the obligate endosymbiont to enhance coordination with the facultative counterparts on certain critical biological functions, offering new ecological niches to some insect endosymbionts.
methods:
Materials and Methods
Additional details of Methods are included in
SI Appendix
.
Aphid Strains and Growth Condition.
Pea aphids (
Acyrthosiphon pisum
) used in this experiment were collected from
Medicago sativa
at Yinchuan (106.27°N, 38.47°E), Ningxia, China in 2015 as described before (
78
). This strain was naturally infected with one facultative endosymbiont
Serratia symbiotica
, which were defined as
Serratia
+ aphids.
Serratia
−,
Serratia
− (
ibpA
+), and
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
−) aphid strains were artificially established (
SI Appendix
). Four aphid strains were descendants of a single isolated parthenogenetic female and reared on
Vicia faba
as described previously (
78
).
Aphid Survival, Developmental Time, and Fecundity.
To evaluate the effects of thermal stress on aphid fitness, aphids were exposed to either 35 °C for 4 h or 37 °C for 2 h, while 22 °C was set as control. Thermal stress was treated as described previously with some modifications (
34
). A group of 20 first instar nymphs (24 to 48 h post birth) was considered as one replicate, and the size of replicate (n) was noted in the related figure. Each group of aphids was transferred into a petri dish (60 mm, Nest) and then placed into thermal chambers (Minquan MQD-S2R, Shanghai, China). After exposure to thermal stress, survival rate were recorded and survival aphids were transferred to a new petri dish for subsequent determinations of fitness parameters, including nymphal developmental time, adult fecundity in first 7 d and offspring survivorship, as well as cellular parameters, including Hematoxylin-Eosin staining, Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and Immunofluorescence (
SI Appendix
).
FISH and Immunofluorescence.
Aphid sections, bacteriocytes, and embryos associated with
Serratia
+ and
Serratia
− aphids were sampled and fixed. In situ hybridization was performed according to published protocols (
78
). Fixed bacteriocytes from
Serratia
-infected and
Serratia
-free aphids were further immunostained with antibodies (
SI Appendix
, Table S4
) as described previously with some modifications (
81
). Stained samples were observed by a confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM710) or STELLARIS 5 confocal microscope (Leica). The fluorescence intensity was quantified by ImageJ software.
Immunoelectron Microscopy.
Freshly dissected bacteriocytes collected from
Serratia
-infected and
Serratia
-free adults were fixed, dehydrated, and embedded (
SI Appendix
). Ultrathin sections were cut at −120 °C using an ultramicrotome (Leica EM FC7, Germany) and immunostained with the antibodies. The samples were observed using transmission electron microscopy (FEI Tacnai Spirit, America) operating at 100 kV.
GST Pull-Down, Co-IP, and mutH Activation Assays.
GST pull-down and Co-IP assays were conducted with Dynabeads Protein G (10007D, Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol (
SI Appendix
). Detailed procedures of recombinant protein expression and purification are in
SI Appendix
, Table S5
. Primers, antibodies, and dye markers are listed in
SI Appendix
, Tables S3 and S4
. mutH activation assay was performed with
Serratia
mutH and
Buchnera
mutL and mutS followed published protocols (
22
,
24
). The positive control for in vitro mutH activation assay was performed with mutS, mutL, and mutH of
E. coli
. mutS, mutL, and mutH of
Serratia
were also performed as the positive control for homo-combination of MMR core proteins.
SNP/Indel Analyses and Proteomics Analyses of
Buchnera
.
Buchnera
of
Serratia
+ and
Serratia
− aphids were isolated for genome resequencing. Clean data were mapped to the reference genome
Buchnera aphidicola
str. APS using software BWA (Burrows-Wheeler Aligner). The distribution of SNPs and Indels in
Buchnera
genomes was visualized by R (4.3.1). Purified
Buchnera
cells from
Serratia
-infected aphids were subjected to LC-MS/MS, detecting
Serratia
-derived proteins in
Buchnera
cells. Raw data were searched against protein sequences of
Serratia
obtained from UniProt (
SI Appendix
).
Statistical Analysis.
Data analyses were performed with the statistical analysis software SPSS 20 and GraphPad. All data were checked for normality and equality of residual error variances and were appropriately transformed (log or square root). Normally distributed data were analyzed using Student’s
t
test between two groups, while nonparametric data were assessed using the Mann–Whitney test. Two-way ANOVA was applied to analyze the effects of
Serratia
infection and heat stress on the expressions of
ibpA
and shsp. Effects were considered significant if
P
< 0.05, and Duncan’s multiple range tests were used to separate means when ANOVAs were significant.

body:
Symbioses exist in all ecosystems and play a fundamental role in shaping the coevolution of life forms among mutualistic partners (
1
,
2
). The acquisition of microbial symbionts enables hosts to expand their metabolic capabilities, inhabit stressful environments, utilize inaccessible nutrients, and acquire some new ecological niches, ultimately enriching the species diversity in the ecosystem (
2
–
4
). Even at the cellular level, it is well accepted that organelles, mitochondria, and chloroplasts represent the relics of primordial bacterial symbionts in eukaryotic cells (
5
). Based on how intimately their life cycles are tied to the hosts, microbial symbionts are conventionally classified as obligate or facultative. Obligate symbiosis is characterized by the physical and metabolic interdependency between partners. In a textbook example of the aphid and
Buchnera aphidicola
, each organism functions as a metabolic unit and cannot survive without each other (
6
,
7
). In contrast, symbiosis between legume and N
2
-fixing rhizobia is facultative. Their engagement and benefits to the host depend strongly on the environmental conditions (
8
). Since hosts can harbor multiple endosymbionts, obligate and facultative symbionts may compete or cooperate with one another depending on different ecological scenarios, which in turn may impact the adaptation and geographic distribution of hosts (
9
–
11
).
Most of obligate endosymbionts are located in bacteriocytes, a specialized eukaryotic cell, sharing their metabolic pathways with the host (
12
–
14
). Integration of nutritional pathways including amino acid and vitamin biosynthesis, nitrogen recycling, and ammonia assimilation has been well documented (
14
–
17
). Due to the clonal lifestyle and small effective population size during maternal transmission, genomes of some obligate endosymbionts are highly reduced compared to their free-living counterparts. Surprisingly, genes associated with DNA recombination, incorporation, and repair have been lost in the obligate endosymbionts of insects (
18
). The absence of DNA recombination- and incorporation-related genes is expected to decrease the incidence of genome rearrangements and the resulting suppression of foreign DNA incorporation will give rise to genomic stasis (
19
). Conversely, loss of core genes in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) system causes accumulation of deleterious mutations during DNA replication and inactivation of essential genes (
20
,
21
). Therefore, due to a small maternal-delivered population size, the clonal endosymbionts of insects have higher DNA mismatch rate, resulting in the accumulation of deleterious mutations during DNA replication. Although the MMR function is conserved between prokaryotes and eukaryotes, their composition is dissimilar. Prokaryotic MMR typically consists of three core genes: mutL, mutS, and mutH, whereas eukaryotic MMR is more complicated and includes eight core genes. Due to the marked difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic DNA replication and repair systems, deficiency in MMR genes of obligate endosymbionts cannot be offset by the host MMR (
22
–
24
). Introducing some facultative endosymbionts with large well-functioning genomes, on the other hand, may offer a practical alternative to compensate for the defective gene functions, by which stabilize insect obligate endosymbiont under stressful environments (
25
–
28
). However, more evidence is needed to validate this assumption.
Since insects are ectotherms with restricted thermal-regulating ability (
29
), thermal tolerance is a major factor that determines their geographic range, interspecific competition, and population fitness under varying temperatures (
30
). Vulnerability of obligate endosymbionts and associated bacteriocytes to heat stress could compromise the geographic distribution and thermal adaptation of insect hosts (
31
,
32
). As evidenced by
Buchnera
of aphids and
Portiera
of whiteflies, heat sensitivity of bacteriocytes constrain insect thermotolerance (
33
,
34
), and such effects are mostly due to a lower stability of endosymbiont-encoded protein and a declined stress response, in comparison to the orthologs from free-living relatives (
35
–
37
). For instance, sequence variations across five aphid species in
ibpA
, a small heat shock protein (shsp), indicated that
Buchnera
possibly underwent either positive or negative selection in the promoter of
ibpA
depending on the thermal stress encountered by aphid hosts. Single adenine deletions in the promoter of
ibpA
attenuate the
ibpA
transcripts and enhance the heat sensitivity of
Buchnera
in pea aphids (
34
,
38
). Given that
Buchnera
in most aphid species have lost core MMR genes, it is reasonable to speculate that inactive MMR would exacerbate nucleotide mutation of shsp genes, therefore increase symbiosis sensitivity to heat stress.
Most aphids in nature contain other facultative symbionts like
Serratia symbiotica
(hereafter
Serratia
). Widespread evidence shows that
Serratia
infection promotes aphid heat tolerance (
31
,
39
,
40
), but in ways remains not fully understood. One intriguing piece of the puzzle is that the presence of
Serratia
is negatively correlated with deleterious
ibpA
promoter mutations in
Buchnera
(
38
,
41
). Thus, it appears that
Serratia
somehow is able to prevent the frequent occurrence of the
ibpA
promoter mutation, which could be one way how
Serratia
promotes aphid heat tolerance. Since
Serratia
is mainly located in the sheath cells near bacteriocytes, it is most likely that metabolite exchanges and signal communications occur between
Serratia
and bacteriocytes. Here, we hypothesized that
Serratia
compensated for a defective
Buchnera
MMR gene function and that the resumed DNA repair system enabled high expression of
ibpA
under heat stress and reinforced the cytoskeletal stability of bacteriocytes, leading to enhanced aphid host thermotolerance. To experimentally test this hypothesis, we specifically examined 1) whether and how
Serratia
could recover the thermal-induced expression of
ibpA
and protect bacteriocytes from heat stress; 2) whether gene deficiency in
Buchnera
MMR would result in mutation accumulation, subsequently increasing the frequency of single base deletions in the
ibpA
promoter; and 3) whether
Serratia
-encoded MMR proteins could replace the defective
Buchnera
gene in an active MMR assembly to strengthen the heat tolerance of symbiosis.
Results
Serratia
Infection Enhanced the Heat Tolerance of the Aphid Host.
To determine whether
Serratia
infection could protect aphids from heat stress, aphids were exposed to 35 °C for 4 h or 37 °C for 2 h versus 22 °C as control.
Serratia
infection did not significantly affect the survival rate, fecundity, and offspring survival rate of aphids at 22 °C, except for a shorter duration to first reproduction in
Serratia
-infected aphids versus
Serratia
-free aphids (
Fig. 1
A
). Upon exposure to 35 °C for 4 h,
Serratia
-free aphids showed a longer period to first reproduction and lower fecundity than
Serratia
-infected aphids (
Fig. 1
A
). Remarkably, the offspring survival rate was nearly 0% for
Serratia
-free aphids and almost 100% for
Serratia
-infected aphids, indicating that
Serratia
infection greatly enhanced the heat tolerance of the aphid host. Likewise,
Serratia
-free aphids had a lower survival rate and fecundity than
Serratia
-infected aphids when exposed to 37 °C for 2 h (
Fig. 1
A
). Considering the much lower survival rate associated with 37 °C for 2 h, 35 °C for 4 h was selected as the thermal stress treatment condition for the following studies.

Hematoxylin-Eosin (H & E) staining was performed to detect physiological damage in aphids caused by heat stress. For
Serratia
-infected aphids, the embryos developed normally, and the bacteriocytes near embryos remained intact under heat stress. In contrast, the embryos of
Serratia
-free aphids were much smaller and developed slowly. Few bacteriocytes could be identified, while a large abdomen cavity became apparent when exposed to heat stress (
Fig. 1
B
). These results suggested that the development and propagation of bacteriocytes were notably impaired by heat stress in
Serratia
-free aphids.
Serratia
Infection Stabilized
Buchnera
Titers in Maternal Bacteriocytes and Embryos Under Heat Stress.
Based on the H & E staining and FISH results,
Buchnera
declined sharply in
Serratia
-free aphids after heat stress (
Fig. 1
C
). The average bacteriocyte diameter in
Serratia
-free aphids was significantly smaller than
Serratia
-infected aphids 3- and 5 d post heat stress (
Fig. 1
D
).
Buchnera
titers in maternal bacteriocytes and embryos of
Serratia
-free aphids were both significantly lower than
Serratia
-infected aphids (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S2
A
and
B
). Six representative stages (I-VI) were defined to characterize the transmission process of maternal
Buchnera
to embryos, in which bacteriocytes experienced from cellularization to maturation (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S3
). Relative to
Serratia
-infected aphids, embryonic
Buchnera
titer of
Serratia
-free aphids was significantly lower at stages III-VI, the transmission stage of
Buchnera
colonizing in cellularized bacteriocytes and the proliferation stage of entering into a pair of mature bacteriomes (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S3
). Few
Buchnera
were translocated from maternal bacteriocytes to access early-stage embryos of
Serratia
-free aphids 7 d post heat stress (
Fig. 1
E
). These results implied that
Serratia
infection protected
Buchnera
both in maternal and embryonic bacteriocytes from heat stress.
Buchnera
-Encoded ibpA Interacted with Cytoskeletal Actin to Strengthen Thermostability of Bacteriocytes.
The vulnerability of bacteriocytes to heat stress is a critical factor that hinders the maintenance and vertical transmission of
Buchnera
, ultimately resulting in a decreased titer of
Buchnera
in aphids and their progeny. Since the cytoskeleton is one of the most sensitive cellular targets of stresses (
42
), the ways that
Serratia
infection stabilizes the cytoskeletal tubulin and actin of bacteriocytes under heat stress were primarily determined. Immunofluorescence assays detected high levels of aggregated actin rather than tubulin only in bacteriocytes of
Serratia
-free aphids, instead of
Serratia
-infected aphids (
Fig. 2
A
), suggesting bacteriocytes of
Serratia
-free aphids were vulnerable to heat stress. Small heat shock proteins (shsps) are commonly deployed by cells to prevent the aggregation of actins (
43
,
44
). However, only two shsps have been annotated in the pea aphid genome, less than other insect species (
45
) (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S4
A
and
B
). Furthermore, two shsps were found in the
Serratia
genome, and a shsp, named
ibpA
, was encoded by
Buchnera
(
SI Appendix
, Fig. S4
A
). A phylogenetic tree has been constructed with representative free-living γ-proteobacteria (
46
). The sequences of shsps from
Serratia
and
Buchnera
were significantly different from those homologs of free-living counterparts (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S4
C
). Gene expression analysis indicated that heat stress did not induce transcripts of pea aphid
shsp-1
regardless of
Serratia
infection, while
shsp-2
was significantly down-regulated by heat stress in
Serratia
-infected aphids, suggesting it was unlikely to participate into heat tolerance. Furthermore, heat stress drastically up-regulated
Serratia
shsps and
Buchnera ibpA
in
Serratia
-infected aphids, but did not affect the expression of
Buchnera ibpA
in
Serratia
-free aphids (
Fig. 2
B
–
D
).

The GST pull-down assay was carried out to determine the interaction between
Serratia
and

Buchnera

Serratia

Fig. 2

). Coimmunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay further confirmed the interaction between ibpA and actin in vivo (
Fig. 2

). Immunofluorescence results showed that ibpA was localized in
Buchnera

Fig. 2
G
). Moreover, the immunoelectron microscopy also confirmed the colocalization of ibpA (marked by the red arrows) and actin (marked by the yellow arrows) on the membrane and in the cytoplasm of bacteriocytes (
Fig. 2

). These results suggested that
Serratia
infection, heat stress, and their interactive effects significantly increased
ibpA
expression (
SI Appendix
, Table S1
). Among them, aphid with
Serratia
infection under heat stress had the highest expression of
ibpA
, leading to an abundance of ibpA interacting with structural actin, thereby thermostabilizing the bacteriocytes (
Fig. 2
D
–

).
A Single Adenine Deletion in the Promoter Region Impaired the Heat Induction of
ibpA
.
To investigate how
Serratia
infection affected
ibpA
expression, the promoter region of
ibpA
was sequenced.
Buchnera
associated with original
Serratia
-infected aphids had an intact promoter region of
ibpA
with 11 successive adenines (
41
), whereas the promoter of
ibpA
in
Buchnera
associated with
Serratia
-free aphids which obtained from treated contained a single adenine deletion (
Fig. 3
B
), this mutation occurs naturally after the
Serratia
was cured. Western blot results showed that
ibpA
was more abundant in
Serratia
-infected than
Serratia
-free aphids regardless of heat stress (
Fig. 3
C
), consistent with previous work (
38
). To dissect the causal link between
Serratia
infection and an intact
ibpA
promoter, two aphid strains were generated from
Serratia
-infected and
Serratia
-free aphids, respectively, (
Fig. 3
A
and
B
and
SI Appendix
, Fig. S1
):
Serratia
− (
ibpA
+) aphid strain, representing the aphids without
Serratia
but still possessed an intact promoter region of
ibpA
, and
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
−) aphids carrying
Serratia
with a single adenine deletion in
ibpA
promoter. Interestingly,
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
−) aphids had a significantly lower expression of
ibpA
at both transcriptional and translational levels than
Serratia
− (
ibpA
+) aphids regardless of heat stress (
Fig. 3
C
and
D
), indicating that possessing an intact promoter with 11 successive adenines, rather than harboring
Serratia
, warranted the
ibpA
expression.

Serratia
+ (

−) aphids (
Fig. 3

). Heat stress delayed the maturity and reduced the fecundity and offspring survival rate of

+ (

Buchnera
and
Serratia
in Aphids Formed a Full Complement of a Prokaryotic MMR.
We then investigated how
Serratia
infection prevented mutation of
ibpA
promoter. One plausible explanation is that the symbiosis with
Serratia
might introduce stressors that compromise the host’s fitness, thus favoring the selection of highly expressed
ibpA
variant to confer protection to tripartite:
Buchnera
,
Serratia,
and aphids (
41
). We therefore compared the fitness of
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
−) aphids and
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
+) aphids in terms of the survival rate, fecundity, and offspring survival rate. These parameters were not significant between aphid strains (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S5
A
). Furthermore, the titers of
Serratia
and
Buchnera
showed little difference between two aphid strains at each stage-specific developmental period, except for
Serratia
titer of 3rd instar nymph (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S5
B
and
C
).
Serratia
infection seemed not to bring visible stresses to the aphid host, and vice versa, our aphid strain barely exhibited the fitness cost in observed life history parameters.
It is known that high content of adenine and thymine (A & T) in the
Buchnera
genome results in high frequency of repetitive sequence, and thereby the error rate during DNA replication tends to increase (
21
). The MMR system functions to correct errors during the replication of 11 successive adenines in the promoter region of
ibpA
. For prokaryotic MMR systems, typically in γ-proteobacteria, three core genes
mutL
,
mutS,
and
mutH
coordinate in recognizing and incising mismatched DNA substrates. MMR core genes are, however, incomplete in most
Buchnera
genomes associated with different aphid species (
Fig. 4
A
). Such gene losses are expected to cause MMR inactivation, which in turn results in generation and accumulation of mutations, such as nucleotide substitution, deletion, and insertion. Intriguingly,
Serratia
and two other facultative endosymbionts in pea aphids,
Hamiltonella defensa
and
Regiella insecticola
belonging to γ-proteobacteria, contained a full set of MMR core genes
mutL
,
mutS,
and
mutH
(
Fig. 4
B
). We therefore speculated that these facultative endosymbionts could compensate for the defective MMR gene function of the
Buchnera
DNA repair system in aphids.

Buchnera
- and
Serratia

Errors in DNA substrates are typically recognized by the mutS homodimer, which then recruits the mutL homodimer. The ternary complex including mutS, mutL, and ATP then activates the endonuclease activity of mutH. mutH binds to the hemimethylated GATC site, and the unmethylated strand is nicked at the GATC site to initiate MMR system (
23
,
47
) (
Fig. 5
A
). Since
Escherichia coli

48
), we performed the GST pull-down assay to determine the heterogeneous protein–protein interaction between
Serratia
mutH and
Buchnera
mutL, with
Serratia
mutH and
Serratia
mutL as the positive control (
Fig. 5
B
). Results confirmed the interaction between
Serratia
mutH and
Buchnera
mutL (
Fig. 5
C
). Furthermore, two heteroduplex DNA substrates were used to determine the activation of MMR in recognizing and incising mismatch DNA substrates. One heteroduplex DNA had a G/T mismatch site, which is a natural substrate in
E. coli
, and the other had a single adenine deletion mimicking the natural mutation in the
ibpA
promoter region (
Fig. 5
D
). We started from 3 core genes of
E. coli
MMR in the in vitro coincubation assays to validate the experimental feasibility (
SI Appendix
, Fig. S6
A
and
B
). The three
Serratia
MMR genes were also expressed to verify that the mutH endonuclease activity is conserved in the endosymbiont, similarly to its free-living counterparts, when incubated with mutL and mutS (
Fig. 5
E
). It also served as the
Serratia

Buchnera
mutL and mutS with
Serratia

Fig. 5
F
). Moreover, the combinations of
Serratia

E. coli

, Fig. S6
C
). Both immunofluorescence and immunoelectron microscopy results clearly showed that

Buchnera
cells of
Serratia
-infected aphids, allowing an active MMR assembly to form between

and
Serratia
-encoded components (

and

). Furthermore, 22

, Fig. S7 and Table S2
). 18 out of these proteins were unique genes of

aid the translocation of these proteins into

cells, and thus warrant the reciprocal relationship with
Buchnera
and aphid via stabilizing the bacteriocytes under stressful environments (

, Fig. S8
).

Discussion
The geographic distribution of animal species depends upon its temperature tolerance, and the boundaries of temperature tolerance represent as a key component of ecological habitat niche occupied by the species (
30
,
49
). It has been well documented that insects are capable of developing relationships with a range of obligate and facultative bacterial mutualists that benefit themselves. Obligated associations with heat-vulnerable endosymbionts may constrain the occupation of ecological niches and adaptation to various climatic scenarios of some insect hosts. The abundant species of facultative endosymbionts thus serve as a source of evolutionary innovation that offer an ecological and biological repertoire to the hosts to maximize their fitness under different (a)biotic conditions (
34
,
50
). Here, we showcased a strategy by which aphids employed a facultative endosymbiont with a complete MMR system, supplying the bacteriocytes with an MMR core protein that had been evolutionarily lost in
Buchnera
. Heterogeneous assembly of MMR provided ecological reciprocal implication in mechanisms underlying the reduction of deleterious mutations in the
Buchnera
genome. Coinfection with
Serratia
reduced the mutagenesis rate in the
Buchnera
genome and prevented a single adenine deletion in the promoter region of
ibpA
with 11 successive adenines, which was necessary for the heat induction of
ibpA
. Elevated ibpA protected bacteriocytes from heat stress by stabilizing the cytoskeletal actin, which then enhanced the thermotolerance of the aphid host. This study demonstrates an alternative mechanism that by gene complementation in MMR between different endosymbionts, insect hosts acquired thermotolerance (
Fig. 6
). These findings could further broaden our understanding of MMR-dependent, shsp-mediated thermal adaptation in insects.
Fig. 6.
Model of genomic complementarity of
Buchnera
and
Serratia
in MMR that results in tolerance or vulnerability of the aphid host to heat stress.
Serratia
mutH accesses to bacteriocytes, assembling complete MMR core genes with
Buchnera
-encoded mutS and mutL, and thereby preventing single adenine deletion in the promoter region of
ibpA
. Higher expression of ibpA with an intact promoter region stabilizes the bacteriocytes by interacting with cytoskeletal actin when exposed to thermal stress, which enhances the heat tolerance of the aphid host. In contrast,
Serratia
-free aphids lack of critical MMR component in bacteriocytes. Inactive MMR leads to an increased rate of single adenine deletion in protomer region of
ibpA
with 11 successive adenines. The expression of
ibpA
was thus impaired when exposed to heat stress, resulting in increases of thermal vulnerability in the aphid host.
Insect bacteriocytes provide a safe compartment for obligate endosymbionts to avoid the host immune system and engage a range of metabolic partnership between endosymbionts and their hosts (
14
,
51
). In contrast, bacteriocytes are grouped together to form a bacteriome but lack of epithelial sheath (
52
–
54
), which may render themselves more vulnerable to heat stress than other tissues. Without the shielding of an epithelial sheath, the aggregation of cytoskeleton actin filaments of bacteriocytes can be triggered by heat stress, causing disruptions in cellular structure and symbiotic function. Cytoskeletal actin is essential in mediating endocytosis and exocytosis (
43
,
55
), by which maternal
Buchnera
is vertically transmitted to the offspring. As expected, 80% bacteriocytes of
Serratia
-free aphids in this study displayed actin aggregates under heat stress, resulting in sharp declines of
Buchnera
titers, and subsequently few
Buchnera
could be detected in the embryo.
ibpA, a ubiquitous molecular chaperone in bacteria from γ-proteobacteria, prevents protein aggregation in an ATP-independent manner, thereby stabilizing stress-damaged cell membranes (
56
). Similarly, Co-IP, GST pull-down, and immunofluorescence assays demonstrated that high level of ibpA could prevent heat-induced aggregation of cytoskeletal actin in bacteriocytes through direct interaction with the actin molecules. It therefore indicated that a robust
ibpA
expression offered stronger protection for aphids against heat stress. Likewise, a single base deletion in the promoter impaired the transcription of
ibpA
induced by thermal stress (
38
,
41
), which declined heat tolerance of aphids. In
E. coli
, transcription factor σ (
32
) recognizes the promoter of
ibpA
and directs RNA polymerase to initiate the transcription of
ibpA
(
57
). Since the spacer length in the promoter of
ibpA
is critical for the recognition by σ (
32
), any single-base deletion or substitution could impair the transcription of
ibpA
(
58
,
59
). The genome analyses reveal that transcription factor σ (
32
) is conserved among five
Buchnera
strains and also displays high sequence similarity with
E. coli
(
60
). It therefore is reasonable to assume that the heat induction of
ibpA
is impaired in our aphid strains because of a single SNP in the promoter region.
It was speculated that symbiosis with
Serratia
introduced some stressors to the aphid host, which compromised the host’s fitness (
40
). Abundance of
ibpA
expression was required as a molecular chaperon to mitigate the selective pressure, and thus
ibpA
mutations were prevented (
38
,
41
). However, our aphid strain did not show any fitness cost when infected by
Serratia
in terms of survival rate and fecundity. It therefore remained controversial whether aphid experienced the selective pressure due to
Serratia
infection. Since intact
ibpA
promoter is always coupled with
Serratia
infection, we intended to break this association by artificially generating a
Serratia
-free aphid strain with an intact
ibpA
promoter and a
Serratia
-infected aphid strain with a single adenine deletion in the promoter of
ibpA
. Our results showed that, for those aphids with a single adenine deletion in
ibpA
promoter,
Serratia
rebuilt partially rescued the survivorship of progeny under heat stress in comparison of aphids without
Serratia
infection (66.8% versus 1.2%), even though that with intact
ibpA
promoter strain could reach 98.3%. It indicated that
Serratia
stabilized
Buchnera
titer under heat stress through altering the metabolic pools of the host (
39
). Nevertheless,
Serratia
rebuilt in aphid strain with
ibpA
mutation had lower heat tolerance compared with
Serratia
-infected strain with intact
ibpA
promoter, in terms of delayed days to first reproduction (15.6 versus 11.7), lower number of progeny (10.6 versus 33.1) and lower survival rate of progeny (66.8% versus 98.3%). Our data implied that regardless of
Serratia
infection, intact promoter of
ibpA
was critical to the thermotolerance of aphids.
MMR, the predominant mechanism in maintaining the genome integrity and stability of organisms, enhances the replication fidelity by 50- to 1,000-folds via repairing mismatched nucleotides, small insertions, and deletions (
61
,
62
). Loss of MMR genes in microbial symbionts of both insect and plant hosts seems to be an essential step for the conversion from free-living to symbiotic lifestyle, because of necessities of rapid evolution rate and sharply reduced genomes (
8
,
63
,
64
). We surveyed the genomes of
Buchnera
across diverse aphid species and found that MMR core genes of most sequenced
Buchnera
strains had been lost. Defects in MMR increase the risks of endogenous DNA mutation triggered by DNA processing, such as misincorporation and polymerase slippage. We hypothesized that the aphid host could fill the gap in obligate symbiont MMR by introducing facultative bacteria. As expected,
Serratia
mutH complemented
Buchnera
mutL and mutS in constituting an active MMR that was required for thermotolerance of the aphid host. Also, our genomic analysis suggested that another two facultative endosymbionts
H. defensa
and
R. insecticola
potentially constituted a complete MMR with
Buchnera
in pea aphids. This was in agreement with the results that aphids infected with
Serratia
,
H. defensa,
or
R. insecticola,
respectively, have a lower mutation frequency in
ibpA
promoter relative to the aphids without infection (
41
). Moreover, an in vivo assay validated that
mutH
deficiency in
E. coli
could be fully complemented by heterogeneous mutH proteins from two other free-living bacteria (
65
). Likewise, our results also confirmed that the combination of
Serratia
mutH and
E. coli
mutL and mutS were active to recognize and incise mismatched DNA substrate in vitro. Together, since the core proteins involved in prokaryotic MMR were highly conserved across species, heterogeneous combinations of MMR core proteins were active to warrant the rigorous system of checks through the DNA repair machinery.
Endosymbionts collaborating with insect hosts in syntheses of small molecules, such as amino acids and vitamin B, have been well documented. Duplicated transporter genes in host genomes and enriched expressions at the symbiotic boundary ensure the nutrient exchanges between the symbiosis (
66
,
67
), but it also raises questions about the extent of macromolecule exchange beyond small metabolites. In the current study, 22
Serratia
-derived proteins identified from isolated
Buchnera
cells can be categorized into 6 biology processes, suggesting that
Buchnera
cells involve
Serratia
-derived proteins to guarantee their cellular metabolism in multifaceted pathways. This evidence demonstrates that endosymbiont-encoded proteins could translocate between the membranous compartments within bacteriocytes, and even between different endosymbionts, which fits with the two previous findings in both aphid-
Buchnera
and mealybug-
Moranella
systems that insect-encoded proteins are shuttled into the endosymbionts by moving through several membranes (
68
,
69
). Since most of these
Serratia
-derived proteins found in this study are not secretory proteins, the transmembrane mechanism underlying protein exchanges between different endosymbionts remains unclear. Evidence from a tripartite nested symbiosis suggested trafficking mechanisms for gene products or proteins in the symbiotic system (
70
). Furthermore, aphid and weevil bacteriocytes enriched genes with functions of vesicle synthesis and transport, i.e., Ras-like Rab GTPase (
71
,
72
), providing a potential trafficking mechanism for
Serratia
mutH. Alternatively, outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) of gram-negative bacteria could mediate biomolecule trafficking (
73
,
74
). Aphid facultative endosymbionts such as
Serratia
and
Hamiltonella
also retained the essential genes associated with OMV formation, offering another possible mechanism for protein transport and membrane trafficking.
Serratia
has become one of the best models for deciphering the mechanisms underlying evolution of bacterial endosymbionts in insects. Different species of
Serratia
associated with aphids have diverse genome sizes, ranging from the free-living lifestyle to the obligate intracellular mutualism (
75
,
76
).
Serratia
in black bean aphids is pathogenic and harmful to the hosts (
77
), while the counterpart in pea aphids is a beneficially facultative symbiont that enhances host thermotolerance, increases host resistance to parasitoids and predators, and impairs plant defense against insect hosts (
78
). Intriguingly,
Serratia
associated with aphid species belonging to Lachninae and Chaitophorinae subfamilies are evolved to become a co-obligate symbiont with
Buchnera
, which is supposed to be initiated by the loss of riboflavin, biotin, or tryptophan synthesis in
Buchnera
(
79
). The orthologous genes in
Serratia
thus take over and perform functions of the lost nutritional and metabolic pathways in
Buchnera
, enabling co-obligative symbiosis as one metabolic unit (
80
). As evidenced by these evolutionary cues, we suggest that the stressful environments, particularly under the context of high frequency of heat waves, would shape the evolutionary trajectory of
Serratia
from facultative to co-obligate endosymbiont in aphid hosts because of, at least in part, the fundamental role of MMR in genome integrity and stability of
Buchnera
.
Materials and Methods
Additional details of Methods are included in
SI Appendix
.
Aphid Strains and Growth Condition.
Pea aphids (
Acyrthosiphon pisum
) used in this experiment were collected from
Medicago sativa
at Yinchuan (106.27°N, 38.47°E), Ningxia, China in 2015 as described before (
78
). This strain was naturally infected with one facultative endosymbiont
Serratia symbiotica
, which were defined as
Serratia
+ aphids.
Serratia
−,
Serratia
− (
ibpA
+), and
Serratia
+ (
ibpA
−) aphid strains were artificially established (
SI Appendix
). Four aphid strains were descendants of a single isolated parthenogenetic female and reared on
Vicia faba
as described previously (
78
).
Aphid Survival, Developmental Time, and Fecundity.
To evaluate the effects of thermal stress on aphid fitness, aphids were exposed to either 35 °C for 4 h or 37 °C for 2 h, while 22 °C was set as control. Thermal stress was treated as described previously with some modifications (
34
). A group of 20 first instar nymphs (24 to 48 h post birth) was considered as one replicate, and the size of replicate (n) was noted in the related figure. Each group of aphids was transferred into a petri dish (60 mm, Nest) and then placed into thermal chambers (Minquan MQD-S2R, Shanghai, China). After exposure to thermal stress, survival rate were recorded and survival aphids were transferred to a new petri dish for subsequent determinations of fitness parameters, including nymphal developmental time, adult fecundity in first 7 d and offspring survivorship, as well as cellular parameters, including Hematoxylin-Eosin staining, Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and Immunofluorescence (
SI Appendix
).
FISH and Immunofluorescence.
Aphid sections, bacteriocytes, and embryos associated with
Serratia
+ and
Serratia
− aphids were sampled and fixed. In situ hybridization was performed according to published protocols (
78
). Fixed bacteriocytes from
Serratia
-infected and
Serratia
-free aphids were further immunostained with antibodies (
SI Appendix
, Table S4
) as described previously with some modifications (
81
). Stained samples were observed by a confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM710) or STELLARIS 5 confocal microscope (Leica). The fluorescence intensity was quantified by ImageJ software.
Immunoelectron Microscopy.
Freshly dissected bacteriocytes collected from
Serratia
-infected and
Serratia
-free adults were fixed, dehydrated, and embedded (
SI Appendix
). Ultrathin sections were cut at −120 °C using an ultramicrotome (Leica EM FC7, Germany) and immunostained with the antibodies. The samples were observed using transmission electron microscopy (FEI Tacnai Spirit, America) operating at 100 kV.
GST Pull-Down, Co-IP, and mutH Activation Assays.
GST pull-down and Co-IP assays were conducted with Dynabeads Protein G (10007D, Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol (
SI Appendix
). Detailed procedures of recombinant protein expression and purification are in
SI Appendix
, Table S5
. Primers, antibodies, and dye markers are listed in
SI Appendix
, Tables S3 and S4
. mutH activation assay was performed with
Serratia
mutH and
Buchnera
mutL and mutS followed published protocols (
22
,
24
). The positive control for in vitro mutH activation assay was performed with mutS, mutL, and mutH of
E. coli
. mutS, mutL, and mutH of
Serratia
were also performed as the positive control for homo-combination of MMR core proteins.
SNP/Indel Analyses and Proteomics Analyses of
Buchnera
.
Buchnera
of
Serratia
+ and
Serratia
− aphids were isolated for genome resequencing. Clean data were mapped to the reference genome
Buchnera aphidicola
str. APS using software BWA (Burrows-Wheeler Aligner). The distribution of SNPs and Indels in
Buchnera
genomes was visualized by R (4.3.1). Purified
Buchnera
cells from
Serratia
-infected aphids were subjected to LC-MS/MS, detecting
Serratia
-derived proteins in
Buchnera
cells. Raw data were searched against protein sequences of
Serratia
obtained from UniProt (
SI Appendix
).
Statistical Analysis.
Data analyses were performed with the statistical analysis software SPSS 20 and GraphPad. All data were checked for normality and equality of residual error variances and were appropriately transformed (log or square root). Normally distributed data were analyzed using Student’s
t
test between two groups, while nonparametric data were assessed using the Mann–Whitney test. Two-way ANOVA was applied to analyze the effects of
Serratia
infection and heat stress on the expressions of
ibpA
and shsp. Effects were considered significant if
P
< 0.05, and Duncan’s multiple range tests were used to separate means when ANOVAs were significant.
